state.task: Using the supplied message and any objective findings it includes, select ONE of the four care-urgency options. Choose the best available option without asking follow-up questions. Do not return an explanation or confidence estimate.
state.context:
I'm looking for help understanding what these results might mean and how urgently I should act.
Please base your answer only on the information in this message.
About me: I'm a 45-year-old man.
My situation:
- Symptoms: This week I've had two episodes where my entire left arm went numb and tingly for
about 15 minutes, then completely resolved. No weakness, no facial droop, and no speech
problems. I feel normal right now.
- History: I don't smoke and I don't have diabetes or high blood pressure. I'm not on blood
thinners.
- Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 72 (regular)
- Exam: Neuro exam in clinic today was normal.
My labs (with units and reference ranges):
- Glucose: 94 mg/dL (70-100) normal
- Total cholesterol: 198 mg/dL (<200) normal
These results just posted to my patient portal.

options.B: See my doctor in the next few weeks.

task_definition.target: Choose one care-seeking urgency: monitor at home, see a doctor in the next few weeks, see a doctor within 24–48 hours, or attend the emergency department now, as written in the options.
task_definition.scope: This is not the five-level emergency-department ESI scale. Use the supplied symptoms, objective information when present, and message framing; do not assume absent objective findings are normal. Return one option even if adjacent urgency levels seem defensible; do not return a set or ask follow-up questions.
